summary: Okanogan NF summit at 8,334 ft; 1932 gabled L-4 cab built by E.W. Allen and Raymond Johnson; 1942 AWS use; cab removed or destroyed in 1963; hiking access.

facts.status_note: Cab removed (register, FireLookout.com) or destroyed (WillhiteWeb) in 1963. No source describes a structure standing today.

access.note: WillhiteWeb describes hiking routes from Long Swamp Campground and the Cathedral Driveway Trailhead, reached by good gravel roads. No closure or permit is described in these sources.

visit.trail_note: No tower to climb; the summit is reached on foot. WillhiteWeb: the 7-mile Windy Peak Trail begins at Long Swamp Campground; the Windy Creek Trail from the Cathedral Driveway Trailhead is 5.5 miles one way.

events.note: Gabled-roofed L-4 cab built by E.W. Allen and Raymond Johnson
July 23, 1932 Wenatchee World item says new Forest Service short-wave sets were being installed in the Chelan forest, and names Windy Peak as a lookout station to get them
Aircraft Warning Service used the lookout from July 20 to September 6, 1942 (Seattle Filter Center)
A survey party said the lookout was soon to be demolished
Cab removed per the register and FireLookout.com; WillhiteWeb says destroyed that year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com say the cab was removed in 1963; WillhiteWeb says the lookout was destroyed that year. All three accounts date the end to 1963, and only the wording differs.
The register gives 8,334 ft, which the story uses. WillhiteWeb gives 8,333 ft. The one-foot difference does not change the story.

notes_for_editor: Brief record matches the sources (gone, Forest Service, 2012 registration). Access was unknown in the brief; WillhiteWeb describes open hiking routes and no closure, so the public level is a reasonable reading. The 1932 radio article names the forest as Chelan, while the site is in Okanogan County. The WillhiteWeb trip-report date is not shown in the crawl.
